fact_text: Gross refining margin is the price spread between a refined product and crude oil, and globally it is set by supply and demand for each product.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Over the long run, diesel margins sit around $15 per barrel above crude, petrol around $8-10 above, and furnace oil around $20 below crude.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A typical Pakistani refinery's output is roughly 35% diesel, 30% furnace oil, 20% petrol and 15% other products such as jet fuel and bitumen, which earn close to zero margin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Blending all product margins, an average Pakistani refinery earns a gross margin of about $4 per barrel on imported crude.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Chemicals cost a refinery about $2 per barrel, and salaries plus electricity about $1 per barrel, which leaves roughly $1 per barrel of profit after costs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A 7.5% deemed duty on diesel is added to the local pump price and protects local refiners; in the analyst's worked example it lifts after-cost profit from about $1 to about $2 per barrel.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Refiners opposed a deemed duty limited to six or seven years because their payback period is longer, so the tenor was extended to 25 years in the policy as described.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The three variables that matter most for a refinery's long-term wealth creation are its diesel share of output, its furnace oil share, and the government's deemed-duty policy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lower furnace oil output and higher diesel output raise refinery profit, so a refinery's process technology largely determines its product mix.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Heavy crude pushes a refinery's furnace oil share toward 45-50%, while light crude or condensate keeps it near 20-30%, so crude quality sets the product mix.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Discounted Russian crude was largely not used by Pakistani refineries, because Russian crude is mostly heavy and would raise furnace oil output enough to cause losses despite the lower price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Local crude output, mostly light crude and condensate from fields in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa such as Nashpa and Tal block, covers roughly a quarter of national consumption.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because fuel prices are uniform nationwide and the government tries to minimise transport costs, refineries closest to the local crude fields in the north receive most of the local crude allocation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Attock Refinery is the northernmost refinery in Pakistan, takes most of the local crude, and runs a furnace oil share of about 20%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A refinery running local crude gets about 15 days of payment credit from the upstream producers OGDC and PPL, which lowers its working-capital financing cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Imported crude runs on a cycle of roughly 30 days (about 15 days shipping plus 15 days of stock), so a refinery must fund crude purchases through bank lines and bears a material financing cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When foreign reserves are weak, Pakistan lacks an IMF programme, or its credit rating slips, banks confirming letters of credit push up the price refiners pay for imported crude, which can wipe out a margin of only a dollar or two per barrel.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Attock Refinery's local-crude advantage could reverse if domestic crude output keeps declining over the next 10-15 years, forcing it to ship imported crude from Karachi to the north and raising transport costs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: P/E ratios should not be applied to refiners directly, because quarterly earnings swing with inventory gains and losses from crude price moves and with abnormal margin spikes; earnings must be normalised first.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Diesel margins spiked to about $40 per barrel during the 2022 Russia-linked war, against a normal $15-20, pushing refiners' earnings to about 3.5 times normal and their P/E ratios near 1.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Normalised refinery profits are several times lower than peak abnormal earnings, so a refiner's normal earnings base supports a P/E of about 4-5 times rather than the near-1 multiple seen at the peak.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A refinery upgrade takes about 4-5 years to build, but the stock market prices the benefit forward as soon as the upgrade is approved.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan Refinery Limited's planned deep-conversion upgrade would expand its refinery from 50,000 to 100,000 barrels per day at a cost of about $2 billion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan prices fuel on Euro-5 imports, so refiners making diesel below Euro-5, or petrol below RON 92, pay a penalty equal to the global price gap, and upgrades remove that penalty.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To judge which refinery gains most from an upgrade, add three savings sources, namely higher diesel share, removal of quality penalties and lower chemical use, and compare the total with the upgrade cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Attock Refinery already holds substantial cash, so it could fund an expansion largely from internal resources or equity rather than rely on heavy bank borrowing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Even with a 75:25 debt-to-equity split, a PRL expansion of this size would need about $500 million of equity, and since profits cannot fund that soon, a rights issue is the likely route.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Sponsor quality matters for refinery partners because an importing refiner relies on the sponsor's credit standing, and minority holders keep only about $1-2 per barrel of margin, so the analyst advised checking a sponsor's reputation and bank standing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Banks are reluctant to open crude letters of credit for private refiners because of past defaults in the oil marketing sector, Hascol Petroleum's default among them, even when refining margins are high.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A proposed rule would give local refineries first right of refusal, so oil marketing companies buy local output before importing, which would let refiners run at higher utilisation with assured offtake.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Invest in Refinery Sector - Big Investment in Refinery Policy' (YouTube transcript, undated)
